hero.title: ELECTRONICS AND COMMUNICATION ENGINEERING IN FRANCE
hero.subtitle: **Study Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE) in France** is a field of study for students interested in electronic devices, wireless communication, telecommunications, signal processing, embedded systems and connected technologies.

overview: **Study Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE) in France** is a field of study for students interested in electronic devices, wireless communication, telecommunications, signal processing, embedded systems and connected technologies.
Related specializations are offered in French universities and engineering schools via electronics, electrical engineering, telecommunication and networks.

Students can opt for **3-year bachelor-level programmes** or longer engineering-school routes in France. It is contingent upon your academic background, the language of instruction you prefer, your budget, and your long-term career goals.
Students can explore these opportunities and know about the requirements involved in getting an education abroad through **Edu Hawk worldwide study abroad guidance**.

sections.title: 8. Accreditation and Recognition of Electronics and Communication Engineering in France**

items: ****Accreditation for ECE in France**** is an important consideration when comparing a three-year bachelor's-level program with a longer engineering-school qualification.
The **Commission des titres d’ingénieur (CTI)** assesses eligible French engineering programs and grants authorization to institutions to deliver the *diplôme d’ingénieur*.
Students should, before enrolling:
* See what precise qualification is awarded.
* Check **CTI accreditation** .
* Ensure the qualification is accepted for entry to relevant postgraduate programs.
* Check the requirements for recognition of degrees in the country where they plan to work.

sections.title: 9. Salary and Job Prospects in Electronics and Communication Engineering in France**

items: Graduates may look for opportunities in **electronics, telecommunications, networking, embedded systems and digital technology**
**Possible career paths:**
* Electronics design or test engineer.
* Telecommunications engineer or technology specialist.
*  Network support or network administrator specialist.
* Embedded systems engineer.
* Signal processing assistant or Signal processing engineer (subject to qualification)
* Radio frequency or wireless systems specialist.
* IoT systems developer.
* Quality assurance and electronics testing specialist.
* Technical support specialist in communication systems.
* Marksheet and completion certificate of class

sections.title: 11. FAQs on Electronics and Communication Engineering Undergraduate in France**

items: Q1. Can Indian students study Electronics and Communication Engineering at the undergraduate level in France?
Yes. **Indian students can study ECE in France** by applying to related bachelor's, BUT, and engineering-school programs if they meet the academic, language and application requirements.
**Q2. Duration of an undergraduate ECE in France**
A **bachelor's degree or BUT** usually takes 3 years. A traditional ** French engineering-school route ** usually lasts five years after secondary school.
**Q3. Are courses in ECE in France taught in English?**

Some engineering programs in France are taught in English, but a lot of electronics and telecommunication bachelors programs are taught in French. Please check the language of instruction of the entire program before applying.
**Q4. What is the cost of undergraduate ECE in France?**

Costs depend on institution and qualification. The differentiated fee for non-EU students under the relevant public-institution rules for **2026–2027** is **€2,902 per year at bachelor level** in the published version. Fees and exemptions vary by institution.
